repo.description:
### Summary

`GET /api/v2/workspaces/{workspace}/external-agent/{agent}/credentials` returns the workspace agent's authentication token and the command used to start an external agent. The endpoint only required read access to the workspace, so users who can view a workspace but are deliberately not allowed to connect to it could retrieve the agent token. The token authenticates as the workspace agent.

> **Note:** Only Premium deployments using external workspaces (a `coder_external_agent` resource in a template) are affected.

### Details

The handler `workspaceExternalAgentCredentials` in `enterprise/coderd/workspaceagents.go` performed no authorization check of its own. The only check came from loading the workspace, which requires `read`. Other endpoints that grant agent-level access, such as the agent coordination endpoint, require `ssh` on the workspace.

Several roles have read access to workspaces but intentionally lack `ssh`: Template Admins, Organization Template Admins, Organization Admins, and the Owner role when `--disable-owner-workspace-access` is set. API tokens scoped to `coder:workspaces.operate` or `coder:workspaces.create` were affected in the same way.

### Impact

A user with one of these roles could retrieve the agent token for another user's external workspace and use it on agent-authenticated endpoints to:

- Read the workspace owner's private Git SSH key.
- Read the workspace owner's external auth (Git provider OAuth) tokens.
- Read the agent manifest, including environment variables and startup scripts from the template.
- Connect as the workspace agent while the real agent is offline, which is the normal state for an external agent before it is installed, and receive the owner's sessions to that workspace.

The attacker needs an authenticated account with one of the roles above. Users the workspace is shared with at `use` or `admin` level already have `ssh` on it and are not affected by this change.

### Patches

The credentials endpoint now requires `ssh` on the workspace and returns `404` without it. Workspace owners, the Owner role, and users the workspace is shared with at `use` or `admin` level keep access.

This is a behavior change: Template Admins, Organization Template Admins and Organization Admins can no longer retrieve the install command for other users' external workspaces, and see an error in the install panel instead. API tokens used for `coder external-workspaces agent-instructions` need a scope that grants `ssh`, such as `coder:workspaces.access`.

This change covers the credentials endpoint. Roles that can update a template can still read agent tokens from that template's workspace build state (`coder state pull`), which is expected behavior.

The fix was backported to the following release lines:

| Release line | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 2.38 (Mainline) | [v2.38.4](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.4) |
| 2.37 (Stable) | [v2.37.8](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.8) |
| 2.36 (Security Support) | [v2.36.11](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.36.11) |
| 2.34 (ESR) | [v2.34.16](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.16) |
| 2.29 (ESR) | [v2.29.24](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.29.24) |

Release lines 2.26 through 2.28, 2.30 through 2.33, and 2.35 are end-of-life and will not receive a patch. Users on these lines should upgrade to a patched release.

### Workarounds

Until you upgrade, limit the Template Admin, Organization Template Admin and Organization Admin roles to trusted users, or avoid templates that use `coder_external_agent`.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31388

### Credits

We'd like to thank a customer security team, @jondavid-black and @Habib0x0 for independently reporting this issue!
repo.summary: Users with only read access to a workspace could retrieve its external agent token
